mcqs.question: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the order of decreasing reactivity among the listed metals?

options.A: Na > K > Ca > Mg > Zn > Fe > Cu > Ag > Au
options.B: K > Ca > Na > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au
options.C: Ca > K > Na > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au
options.D: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au

mcqs.answer: K > Ca > Na > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au
mcqs.explanation: The standard reactivity series in decreasing order is K, Ca, Na, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Ni, Sn, Pb, H, Cu, Ag, Au. Option B matches this sequence exactly, while the other options have metals in the wrong order.

mcqs.question: When a strip of zinc is placed in a solution of copper(II) sulfate, which of the following best predicts the outcome?

options.B: Zinc dissolves and copper metal plates out
options.C: Copper dissolves and zinc metal plates out

mcqs.answer: Zinc dissolves and copper metal plates out
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so zinc atoms lose electrons (oxidise) to form Zn²⁺, while Cu²⁺ ions gain electrons (reduce) to deposit copper metal. Hence option B is correct; the other options contradict the series behavior.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes what happens when a metal that is higher in the reactivity series is placed in a solution of a salt of a metal lower in the series?

options.B: The more reactive metal dissolves, and the less reactive metal precipitates
options.C: The less reactive metal dissolves, and the more reactive metal precipitates

mcqs.answer: The more reactive metal dissolves, and the less reactive metal precipitates
mcqs.explanation: A metal higher in the series can displace a lower‑reactivity metal from its salt solution. The higher metal oxidises (dissolves) and the lower metal is reduced (precipitates). Options A, C and D do not follow this principle.

mcqs.question: Which metal is more reactive: magnesium or iron?

options.D: Reactivity cannot be determined from the given information

mcqs.explanation: In the reactivity series, magnesium appears above iron, indicating it loses electrons more readily and is therefore more reactive. Hence option A is correct; iron is less reactive, and the series provides the needed information.

mcqs.question: The reactivity series is a list that arranges metals in order of their ability to:
mcqs.explanation: The reactivity series ranks metals according to their tendency to undergo oxidation, i.e., to lose electrons. Conductivity, alloy formation, and melting points are unrelated to this specific ordering.

mcqs.question: Which of the following metals will displace copper from a copper(II) nitrate solution?
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is placed above copper in the reactivity series, so it can reduce Cu²⁺ ions to copper metal while Zn itself is oxidised to Zn²⁺. Silver, gold and lead are below copper and cannot cause displacement.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question: Which equation correctly represents the reaction when iron filings are added to copper(II) sulfate solution?
mcqs.explanation: Iron is higher than copper in the series, so it displaces copper. The balanced single‑replacement reaction is Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu. Options B and C are not balanced or chemically valid, and a reaction does occur, ruling out D.

mcqs.question: A student wants to extract copper from its ore using a metal displacement method. Which metal should be used as the reducing agent?
mcqs.explanation: To reduce copper ions, the chosen metal must be higher in the reactivity series than copper. Zinc satisfies this condition, while lead and silver are lower and sodium is unnecessarily reactive and hazardous. Hence zinc is the appropriate choice.
